about: What the picture pipeline draws and how. The style block is the contract: it is sent word for word with every sheet, so sheets made months apart match. Change the style only by adding a new version; tiles record the version they were drawn in. Anything that applies to one sheet only (such as "no people and no animals" for plants) goes in that sheet's `only_for_this_sheet`, never in the shared style.

style.text: Realistic, natural-looking image in the style of a high-quality nature guide or museum catalogue. True-to-life shape, colour and proportion, with fine natural detail. Soft, even daylight with no dramatic shadows. Each subject is shown whole, centred, filling about three quarters of its cell, isolated on a plain white background that is identical in every cell. No text, letters, numbers, labels, borders or frames. Where the subject is a place, such as a river or a hill, show it as a small self-contained piece of landscape with soft edges on the same white background.
style.layout: One image containing a {grid} by {grid} grid of {count} equal square cells. Wide white gaps separate the cells, each gap at least one twentieth of the image width, with no dividing lines. Nothing in one cell touches or crosses into another. Each cell shows exactly one subject, in this order, left to right, top to bottom:
style.approved: by the owner on 2026-10-06, as drafted from his opening words (realistic, nature guide or museum catalogue)
style.size_from_now_on: 2880 px sheets of nine, by the owner's ruling on 2026-10-06: about 2 rupees a tile and masters about 1000 px square. 3072 is refused by the service (8.3 megapixel limit).

dinosaurs_1.only_for_this_sheet: Each cell shows one prehistoric animal only, as a careful, scientifically informed life reconstruction of the kind printed in a museum guide: the whole animal including the tail, seen from the side, in natural, plausible colours. No people, no other animals, no scenery, no skeletons and no fossils.

cells.draw: a huge two-legged meat-eater with a massive deep skull and thick teeth, tiny two-fingered arms, powerful hind legs and a long heavy tail held level; scaly skin
cells.name: Tyrannosaurus rex

cells.draw: as long as T. rex but more lightly built, with a longer, lower, narrower skull, rough ridges above the eyes, and three-fingered arms
cells.look_closely: easily drawn as a second T. rex; check the longer, narrower skull and three fingers
cells.name: Giganotosaurus

cells.draw: a medium-sized two-legged meat-eater with a pair of short horn-like crests in front of the eyes and three-fingered hands with large claws

cells.draw: a long, low, crocodile-like snout with cone-shaped teeth, a tall sail along its back, short hind legs, and a long deep paddle-shaped tail
cells.look_closely: scientists' picture of it has changed; check the paddle tail and short legs

cells.draw: the size of a turkey, covered in feathers with feathered arms and a feathered tail, a long narrow snout, and one raised sickle-shaped claw on each foot
cells.look_closely: science says small and feathered; films show it large and scaly. Your decision which he should see

cells.draw: a four-legged plant-eater with a large bony neck frill, two long brow horns, one short nose horn and a parrot-like beak
